relevance_note: Case report of a girl with NOD2-associated pediatric granulomatous arthritis: 'identified a heterozygous germline missense mutation in NOD2 common in PGA (c.1001G>A, p.Arg334Gln)'; the Discussion also gives individual-level facts about four previously published EOS/BS patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory and every span checked verbatim against the paper by script. Scope: the index patient ('patient', single unnamed case-report patient) plus four previously published people described in the Discussion with at least one individual-level fact (Borzutzky ref (34) infant with EOS; Wong ref (41) 18-year-old woman with EOS; Gedalia ref (38) patient with EOS and hypercalcemia; Teng Lo ref (18) 5-year-old girl with BS, NOD2 c.2123G>A). Refs (41) and (38) had no NOD2 testing but carry an EOS diagnosis, so they are in scope by the diagnosis rule. Hoffmann ref (32) children (three < age 5 'likely examples of PGA', counts only, no diagnosis) and Rose ref (14) registry counts were not given rows. The father ('said perhaps to have dense bones', not evaluated) and the mother (informant only) were not given rows: neither was tested nor described as affected. Labels for literature patients use the superscript reference number as printed, e.g. 'ref (34) patient'. Age at last evaluation '41/2 years' is the converted text of 4 1/2 years (also '21/4 to 41/2 years'); recorded as printed with P4Y6M. Age at onset of the PGA picture is not stated (joint swelling 'during the previous year' before 33 months), so left not reported; early UTIs/VUR and unusual crawl have their own onset ages. Ref (34) infant: checklist dermatitis/uveitis/arthritis marked observed from 'including the classical clinical triad' together with the paper's definition of the triad; ref (34) gives no NOD2 variant, so no variant row. Apparent tensions in the paper: the authors say the patient lacked arthritis ('lacked the classic triad ... arthritis', 'without other signs of arthritis') yet MRI and biopsy show synovitis and the text speaks of 'joint synovitis'; both rows emitted and checklist 'arthritis or joint synovitis' set observed on the synovitis evidence. Rheumatoid factor was normal at 33 months and positive later; ACE was normal at the Research Center (also 99 U/L in Table 1, range 22-108) and later high at 102 U/L: these are changes over time, both rows emitted. Normal findings (ANA, lead, ACE, TRAP, bone ALP, DPD, PTHrP, hepatitis C/HIV) recorded as the excluded abnormality per D-27; 'Mucopolysaccharide screening was unremarkable' and 'normal appearing brain' recorded nothing. Table 1 (single-patient laboratory values) was used only where the text also states the abnormality; table-only out-of-range values (e.g. phosphorus, uric acid, albumin, platelets) were not turned into features. Checklist 'granulomatous nephritis or renal failure' set observed from 'compromised renal function' (creatinine clearance 39 and 49), which the authors attribute to nephrocalcinosis, not nephritis. Publications: cites_prior_report set true because the work was 'Presented In Part' as a published meeting abstract (J Bone Miner Res 32 Suppl 1: S297, 2017).
